channel.description: Recent content in Ai on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expands to Hong Kong
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace multiparty private offers are now expanding to Hong Kong. This lets partners procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers in the Hong Kong market through Marketplace.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
item.description:
GitHub announced a new purpose-built, context-aware model for leaked secret detection as part of Secret Protection. It is intended to improve secret detection in code workflows, including those that involve AI agents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Using Whisper, FFMPEG, and yt-dlp to Analyze Sermons for Red Flags🔥
item.description:
The article describes a toolchain using Whisper, FFmpeg, and yt-dlp to download sermon audio/video, transcribe it, and analyze the text for potentially bigoted or otherwise problematic language. It frames the approach as using AI to review sermons for “red flags.”

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Secure what’s next: Your guide to Microsoft Security at Microsoft Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 security post says the company will highlight an AI-first, end-to-end security platform. The platform is described as covering identities, devices, data, applications, clouds, infrastructure, and AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: Why content extraction still matters in the GenAI era
item.description:
The post argues that as AI models improve, reliable content extraction becomes more important for trustworthy downstream use. It also contrasts Azure Content Understanding and Azure Document Intelligence, and previews what is next.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Migration Agent Skills for assessment, migration, and validation
item.description:
SQL Migration Agent Skills are now generally available to help automate SQL Server to Azure migrations. They provide reusable AI-powered skills for assessment, target selection, migration execution, and post-migration validation.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Build Agentic UI with the new Blazor AI components
item.description:
Microsoft announced new Blazor AI components for building agentic UI in .NET. The components target streamed content, tool use, approvals, shared state, and generative experiences.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: From guidance to action: Security fundamentals that materially reduce risk
item.description:
Microsoft says AI has changed the cybersecurity operating environment and points readers to exposure management guidance with recommended controls. The post emphasizes taking action on security fundamentals to reduce risk.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥AI makes works for itself
item.description:
The note says AI should be used to update tools, and nothing more. It frames the idea as “AI to update tools only.”

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender is described as detecting and disrupting AI-themed phishing, malware, and multi-stage attacks across the attack chain. The post is a Microsoft Security Blog entry dated 2026-09-10.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft reports that invisible Unicode characters, previously used in AI prompt injection, are now being used to hide words from email filters as part of phishing evasion. The technique relies on obfuscating text before parsers process it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Designing product simplicity for the AI era
item.description:
The article asks whether shared design components are sufficient for a seamless product experience, or whether designers need to prioritize simplicity over complexity to create consistency. It frames this as a product design question for the AI era.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: How Uno Platform uses .NET, MCP, and AI to build high quality apps
item.description:
Uno Platform built two MCP servers in C# to let AI agents use real documentation as context and interact with a running cross-platform .NET app. The post describes how .NET, MCP, and AI are combined to support app development and validation.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Routing and Failover for Microsoft.Extensions.AI
item.description:
Microsoft.Extensions.AI adds experimental routing primitives for model/provider selection and failover: RoutingChatClient, SemanticRoutingChatClient, and FailoverChatClient. These support content-based routing, failover handling, and custom routing policies.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Instructions Hygiene – What Frontier Models Still Need You to Say
item.description:
The post says frontier models still need explicit, well-scoped instructions to work reliably. It emphasizes giving the right level of guidance rather than assuming the model will infer missing details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Unity AI Gateway on Azure Databricks
item.description:
Unity AI Gateway is now generally available on Azure Databricks. It provides centralized governance for AI models, agents, tools, and MCP services, with controls for monitoring usage, managing costs, applying guardrails, and enforcing access control.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: Had baby, Back September!
item.description:
The post says the author had a baby in September and will be back later. They also note they won’t be using AI for a while.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: security: ​​Better security starts with better questions
item.description:
Microsoft Security says stronger security decisions come from asking better questions, using trusted AI, and combining AI outputs with human judgment. The post frames this as a way to help leaders make more confident decisions and build more resilient systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Code scanning shows AI security detections on pull requests
item.description:
GitHub code scanning now shows AI-powered security detections on pull requests. The feature expands coverage to languages and frameworks not currently supported by CodeQL.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative
item.description:
Microsoft published its July 2026 Secure Future Initiative progress report, summarizing work on secure foundations, AI-assisted defense, and broader cybersecurity readiness. The provided text is only a brief overview and does not include specific implementation details or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
